tweet_summary: Post claims the DHS funding bill (H.R. 7147) 'allocates $10 BILLION MORE for ICE operations,' passed 220-207, giving ICE 'EVEN MORE money,' with SIX Democrats voting yes.
why_note_decision: The tweet misstates the bill's effect and the vote. The DHS appropriations bill did not give ICE $10 billion more; it kept ICE funding roughly flat, cut funding for enforcement and removal operations, and reduced detention beds versus FY2025 — the opposite of 'EVEN MORE money to boost deportation numbers.' Seven Democrats voted yes, not six. From a 1.5M-follower account at 253k impressions, these are concrete legislative facts worth correcting.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note corrects the bill's effect and the vote count: the DHS funding bill (H.R. 7147, passed 220-207 on Jan 22, 2026) did NOT add $10 billion for ICE — it kept ICE funding roughly flat, cut enforcement-and-removal funding, and reduced detention beds vs FY2025; and SEVEN Democrats voted yes, not six. The note must rebut the '$10 billion more' / 'even more money to boost deportations' framing with the flat/cut reality. A note that only fixes the Democrat count but lets the '$10B more for ICE' claim stand is incomplete; FAIL any note that endorses the '$10 billion more for ICE' framing. Keep tone neutral/bridging.
reference_note: The DHS funding bill (H.R. 7147, passed 220-207) keeps ICE's budget roughly flat rather than adding $10 billion; it cuts funding for enforcement and removal operations and reduces detention beds vs FY2025. Seven Democrats voted yes, not six. https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7147 https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-passes-sprawling-spending-package-democrats-split-ice-funding-rcna255273

fact_check.claim_verdict: Misleading: bill did not add $10B for ICE (kept flat / cut enforcement-removal funding, fewer detention beds); 7 Democrats voted yes, not 6.
fact_check.notes: Congress.gov + NBC confirm 220-207 passage and seven Democratic yes votes (Cuellar, Golden, Gillen, Gluesenkamp Perez, Davis, Suozzi, Gonzalez). Reporting notes Democrats secured cuts to ICE enforcement/removal funding and $20M for body cameras; detention beds capped at 34,000 (a reduction). The '$10 billion MORE' framing is the misleading element. Provisional no_note overweights the partisan 'note not needed' ratings; the factual misstatements justify a note.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.5M-follower account, 253k impressions, on major immigration-enforcement legislation; accurate legislative facts on ICE funding matter for policy-relevant public understanding.
